newsitem.title: GERMANY: German debt starts well, awaits 10-year supply.
newsitem.headline: German debt starts well, awaits 10-year supply.

text.p: German Bunds and futures moved tentatively forward in early trade but dealers said the market would remain relatively subdued ahead of a new issue of 10-year paper due later this session.
Players said the propsect of the new supply had driven noticeable curve steepening in the last few session, with investors wary of the longer-dated maturities.
By 0742 GMT, the 6.0 percent coupon 10-year benchmark Bund due January 2007 was trading at 100.86 for a yield of 5.871 percent, up slightly from its previous close at 100.78 on Monday.
In the futures market, the June DTB contract was nine basis points higher on the day at 100.50, having traded as high as 100.57 in early business.
"There is not an awful lot of flow in the market this morning," said one Bunds trader based at a Dutch bank in London. "The main focus is the new 10-year issue."

"This new supply steepened the two/10-year curve by about three or four basis poinst yesterday, and most of the casg market interest we have seen has been five-years and in, rather than in the 10-year area," he said. The two/10-year yield spread was 229 basis points by 0749 GMT.
Traders said that if the Bundesbank offered the new paper at a reaonable price with a "fairly generous" coupon, the market should absorb the supply fairly well.
Some were looking for a coupon of 5-7/8 to six percent.

Comments from Bundesbank president Hans Tietmeyer, who said late on Monday that he could not rule out a possible delay to Europe's monetary union if major countries did not meet the entry criteria, had little effect on Bunds directly.
But Bunds did benefit on spreads, taking one basis points apiece from gilts and BTPs, and outclassing Swedish bonds to the tune of four basis points in early business.
